parts.note: a sac is a bag-like part of a plant or animal

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the series goes round the royal letter, and the bag comes first.

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer at 20 across, a heater; a kind of heating furnace or drying kiln
the edible bivalve mollusc with a ribbed shell

explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a Church of England parish priest, a kind of clergyman.

clue.text: No right to lark about in support for supplement

indicators.note: no right asks for the letter that abbreviates right to be dropped from the word

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for about inside the word for support

C is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Without permission to fool around, someone turns to a dietary supplement for support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No right' signals dropping R, and 'in' signals the container. 'lark about' reads as one phrase in the surface, but 'about' is split off to give C (circa). 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Folic acid is a B vitamin commonly taken as a dietary supplement, especially in pregnancy.

clue.text: Bang on to be right over Tyneside's incidental perk

parts.note: bangs is the American word for a fringe of hair
be is the verb to be
NE is northeast England, where Tyneside lies
fit means right or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone insists it is fair that Newcastle staff get a perk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'over' only link the pieces. Tyneside, round Newcastle, is in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe benefit is an extra advantage on top of salary, like a company car.

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
a nation is a people

explanation.definitionFit: Tarnation is an old-fashioned, mainly American mild oath, a euphemism for damnation used as a curse.

clue.text: Cut down on volume with healthy eating

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: hale means healthy and strong, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Advice to reduce one's portions as part of a healthy diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts V inside HALE. 'on' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to cut it down to half its size or amount.

clue.text: Support for press baron on rigid preparation

indicators.note: a preparation is something made up from ingredients, so the letters are made up into a new word

explanation.surface: A newspaper baron backs the press with firm preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspaper world of the baron, but it means pressing clothes with an iron. 'preparation' rearranges BARON ON RIGID.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the padded folding stand on which clothes are laid to be pressed with an iron.

indicators.note: the rearranged name covers or wraps round the word for time
redesigned means made over in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the boy reporter's name, with the 's only a possessive
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Tintin's comic gets a new cover for an issue about time travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time Traveller' in quotes looks like one title but splits in two: Time is wordplay and Traveller is the definition. 'redesigned' rearranges the boy reporter's name to ITINNT, and 'cover for' wraps it round the period.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is someone who travels from place to place, a traveller.

clue.text: Polo's so engrossing, or one's not part of the main group

taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.walkthrough: Polo is neither the sport nor Marco Polo but a ring-shaped peppermint sold in Britain. 'engrossing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A minority is the smaller part of a group, those outside the majority.

clue.text: Gag about scripture gets lady in garden upset

clue.text: Action in which the bar is approached with low expectations

clue.text: Bird that's said to play that game?

clue.text: Cooked up old bits about female driver being useless

parts.note: a chauffeuse is a woman chauffeur

explanation.walkthrough: 'being useless' splits as USE-LESS, so the three letters U, S, E drop out of the female driver's title, leaving CHAUFFE. A réchauffé is a dish of warmed-up leftovers.

clue.text: Put forward when maintaining one's equilibrium
